title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: In lanthanide-functionalized [SiW11O39] clusters, redox-inactive Ln3+ can raise photocatalytic HER activity relative to the parent polyoxotungstate, an effect attributed to Lewis acidity rather than Ln-centered redox.
explanation: Mirzaei’s LnW11 (Ln = La, Pr, Dy) clusters were the first lanthanide-functionalized polyoxometalates reported for both homogeneous photocatalytic and heterogeneous electrocatalytic HER, and activity depended on the lanthanide. LaW11 and DyW11 were 40–60% more active photocatalytically than W11.
scope: Ln-functionalized Keggin-derived polyoxotungstates Ln[(pdc)2Ln(H2O)2SiW11O39] for HER.
conditions: Photocatalysis with 470 nm irradiation, [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2, ascorbic acid, and H2O/MeOH (9:1); LaW11 TON 525 and TOF 324 h−1 in Table 1.
caveats: The Lewis-acidity/PCET interpretation is proposed because the chosen Ln ions are redox inactive; it is not a direct spectroscopic proof of the proton-transfer step.
